speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your vertigo. Does the sensation of spinning occur only when you change your head position, or does it happen spontaneously while you are upright?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The sudden onset triggered by bed movement, short duration of 3 minutes, and spontaneous resolution without hearing loss or neurological deficits are classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
